title: Qualcomm Layoffs Reach India Notifications, but Severance Terms Remain Undisclosed
excerpt: Industry estimates put 600 to 1,200 India jobs at risk in Qualcomm's performance-focused global cuts, while the company has confirmed neither the India count nor any severance package.
body:
• Qualcomm is carrying out a performance-focused global workforce reduction, with employee notifications beginning in November 2026 after annual reviews.
  • Industry estimates cited in reporting put 600 to 1,200 India jobs at risk — 3% to 6% of an estimated 20,000-person India workforce — but Qualcomm has not confirmed any India figure.
  • Qualcomm has not publicly disclosed severance terms for India employees; affected workers should wait for their individual official notice rather than rely on estimates.
  • CEO Cristiano Amon described the cuts in an internal memo reported by Reuters on October 20; the memo gave no worldwide headcount.

Qualcomm's global job cuts have reached the notification stage, and for employees in India the central facts are still narrow: notifications were due to begin in November, and the company has not confirmed how many India roles will go or what severance any departing employee will receive.

According to reporting by Trak.in, industry estimates suggest between 600 and 1,200 jobs in India could be affected, equivalent to roughly 3% to 6% of Qualcomm's estimated 20,000 employees in the country. Research firm EIIRTrend reportedly expects the cuts to exceed 1,000, while UnearthInsight estimates a smaller impact of fewer than 3% of the local workforce. Qualcomm did not respond to queries about those estimates and has not officially confirmed the number of positions to be eliminated in India.

What was actually announced

The global plan was set out in an internal memo from chief executive Cristiano Amon, reported by Reuters on October 20. Amon described a performance-focused reduction following the company's annual reviews, with notifications beginning in November. The memo did not disclose the total number of jobs affected worldwide. Qualcomm had about 52,000 employees globally as of September 2025, according to Reuters reporting summarized by The Living Draft.

Qualcomm has described the exercise as intended to build a stronger performance culture. Reporting on the memo says decisions will also consider business priorities, organisational requirements, and employees' skills and expertise — not performance ratings alone.

The severance question

No source reporting on this round has published a Qualcomm severance formula for India — no weeks-per-year figure, no notice-period package, and no confirmed benefits continuation. That absence matters because the cuts are framed as performance-focused: reporting on the announcement notes that actual terms will depend on company policy, individual employment arrangements and applicable law, and that employees should watch for official internal communication on notice periods and any applicable severance benefits. Any specific severance number circulating without a Qualcomm notice or a named source should be treated as unverified.

Why Qualcomm is cutting

The restructuring comes as Qualcomm navigates pressure in its traditional smartphone business. Trak.in reported rising memory chip prices are increasing device costs and putting pressure on demand, and that Qualcomm has warned revenue from Apple-related products could decline faster than previously expected. At the same time, the company is expanding into AI data centres, automotive technology and the Internet of Things, and expects businesses outside smartphones to account for the majority of its chip sales by fiscal 2027, according to the same reporting.

What India employees should watch

For an individual employee in India, there is not yet enough public information to assess the risk to a specific role, team or location — no source has established which offices or departments face the greatest impact. The next confirmed development will be the individual notifications themselves, which carry the role decision, the end date and the terms that apply to that employee. Until then, the 600-to-1,200 range remains an industry estimate, not a confirmed layoff count.
nri_angle: Indian tech employees at Qualcomm face November notifications with an estimated 600 to 1,200 India roles at risk and no disclosed severance terms.
author: Diaspora Desk
